action.name: Switch off lighting when display is turned off
action.value: Windows display off, physical blackout hold, wake, and exact lighting restoration

validation.applyResult: The status-02 brightness-zero response and operator-confirmed physical darkness successfully matched the display-off action.
validation.readbackResult: The zero-frame blackout interval and operator confirmation successfully confirmed the off state.
validation.restorationResult: Synapse successfully restored raw brightness FF and resumed the host frame stream after wake.
validation.restorationReadbackResult: The operator confirmed that the original pad lighting successfully returned after wake.

sanitizedEvidence.summary: After Windows posted monitor power-off, Synapse sent 0F/04 payload 010000 and received a status-02 echo. The operator confirmed that the pad went physically dark.
No 0F/03 host lighting frame occurred between the brightness-zero setter and the wake restoration setter.
On wake, Synapse queried brightness, sent 0F/04 payload 0100FF, received a status-02 echo, and resumed 0F/03 frames 482.48 milliseconds later. The operator confirmed physical restoration.
The pad-only decoded view contained 974 bounded transactions and matched the full-root source hash recorded above.

limitations: The full-root all-devices capture includes unrelated USB traffic; conclusions are limited to the exact VID 1532 PID 0F43 pad address and marker-aligned control transfers.
The capture confirms one 100-percent brightness restoration value; it does not independently validate restoration at every saved brightness.
The display-off sequence confirms blackout and restoration behavior but does not assign the strip's physical origin or direction.
Unplug persistence, sleep and resume behavior, and accepted frame-rate tolerance remain unvalidated.
No OpenBlade lighting write or host-frame replay was performed.

productionAdmission.reason: Display-off brightness and stream behavior are now physically confirmed, but physical strip order and remaining lifecycle and cadence bounds are incomplete.

notes: The capture stopped by the owned sentinel and targeted graceful Ctrl+Break; no USBPcap process remained.
The raw full-root capture, filtered capture, decoded transactions, state, and operator markers remain local and uncommitted.
OpenBlade and the two Razer background services were running after cleanup.
